chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the young boy who has not yet reached puberty (hadith) and his mahr (dowry). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he divorces in accordance with the Sunnah and places the mahr in its rightful place and due share, then there is no problem, and it is valid.'

key_terms.لَمْ يَحْتَلِمْ: Has not yet bed-wet (sign of puberty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorcing a young boy who has not yet reached puberty?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the fiqh of *tabarru'* (gift-based) divorce for a pre-pubescent boy who has not yet reached *bulugh* (puberty), emphasizing that validity hinges on the proper allocation of his mahr. It reflects the Shia juristic view that while the boy lacks full legal capacity, his guardian’s adherence to the Sunnah in managing his financial rights ensures the divorce is sound and permissible.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, and Ali Bin Ibrahim from his father, altogether from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about divorce of the young boy who has yet to bed-wet, and his charity. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he divorces in accordance to the Sunnah (under guidance) and places the charity in its rightful place, so there is no problem, and it is allowed’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “

I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the divorce of a boy who is not mature yet, and his charity. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he divorces according to Sunnah and places charity in the proper place where it rightly belongs, it is not unlawful and it is permissible.’”
